We have the privilege this evening to recognizing Donors' Choice, a national nonprofit organization with over four million donors across the country whose mission is to make it easy for anyone to help a teacher in need. Invites members of the community to support a classroom and build a future. For more than two decades, the organization has made it possible for teachers across the country to design and implement classroom learning experiences that have enhanced the way of children's learning. Over the years, our Royal County public schools teachers

have raised more than $300,000 for nearly 700 classroom projects. This year, in collaboration with the division's Family Council, which includes a parent representative for every school, the division established a formal partnership with Donors' Choice that has provided new opportunities to advance the division's strategic goal of thriving students.

The strategic plan commits the division to facilitate learning experiences ground in high expectations, networks of care, and student curiosity to ensure academic and social-emotional development for all students while eliminating opportunity, access, and achievement gaps.
By supporting teacher projects, every member of our community can join with our teachers in adding authentic, challenging, and relevant and inclusive learning experiences for students.

Community members can support teacher projects seeking funding in total amounts ranging from $140 to $1,700. Requests range from helping to expand learning sources to providing food for students in need to combat bullying or eliminating chronic absenteeism.

Donors have an opportunity to contribute any amount. In many cases, a contribution can be matched by another donor, increasing the value of even a modest gift. The formal partnership offers special and targeted matching funds for equity schools, which includes schools that have populations of 50% or more students who qualify for free or reduced lunch.

Partnership with Donor's Choice offers another pathway to fulfilling all four of the school divisions' value, equity in excellence, family and community and wellness. Community members can gain more information about the partnership and its objectives on the ACPS website.

This evening, we are happy to have Ms. Heidi Gilman-Bennett, Family Council President, who will share information about the progress of the initiative and introduce ACPS educators, Ms. Bridget Sears and Brandy Orshoki, who will highlight Donors' Choice Projects that have offered unique learning opportunities for their students.
